newsitem.title: USA: Rural/Metro Corp to acquire 4 companies.
newsitem.headline: Rural/Metro Corp to acquire 4 companies.

text.p: Rural/Metro Corp said on Thursday it had agreed to acquire four ambulance service providers in southern and midwestern states that generate combined revenue of $10 million annually.
Terms of the agreements were undisclosed. Final deals remain subject to regulatory approval and definitive purchase agreements.
"Our ongoing efforts to expand our regional presence continues as planned," Warren Rustand, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

ProMed Ambulance Service, based in El Dorado, Ark., provides emergency and non-emergency transport in four counties. Its owner and CEO David Lewis will remain with the company as general manager of Rural/Metro's Arkansas service.

Richmond and Regional Ambulance Services, based in Augusta, Ga., provides primarily non-emergency general transport in northeastern Georgia and western South Carolina. It will be merged into the existing Rural/Metro operations.
Rural/Metro also completed acquisitions of two unnamed operations in Muncie, Ind., and Cleveland, Ohio. These acqusitions are being incorporated into existing Rural/Metro regional operations.
